{{short description|Czech mathematician}}
'''Zdeněk Dvořák''' (born April 26, 1981) is a Czech mathematician specializing in [[graph theory]].

Dvořák was born in [[Nové Město na Moravě]].<ref name="cv"/>
He competed on the Czech national team in the 1999 [[International Mathematical Olympiad]],<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.imo-official.org/team_r.aspx?code=CZE&year=1999&column=total&order=desc&gender=hide|title=Czech Republic, 40th IMO 1999|publisher=[[International Mathematical Olympiad]]|access-date=2015-09-16}}.</ref> and in the same year in the [[International Olympiad in Informatics]], where he won a gold medal.<ref>{{citation|url=http://stats.ioinformatics.org/results/1999|title=IOI 1999 Results|publisher=[[International Olympiad in Informatics]]|access-date=2015-09-16}}.</ref> He earned his Ph.D. in 2007 from [[Charles University in Prague]], under the supervision of [[Jaroslav Nešetřil]]. He remained as a research fellow at Charles University until 2010, and then did postdoctoral studies at the [[Georgia Institute of Technology]] and [[Simon Fraser University]]. He then returned to the Computer Science Institute (IUUK) of Charles University, obtained his [[habilitation]] in 2012, and has been a full professor there since 2022.<ref name="cv">{{citation|url=https://iuuk.mff.cuni.cz/~rakdver/cv.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae: Zdeněk Dvořák|access-date=2023-02-10}}.</ref>

He was one of three winners of the 2015 [[European Prize in Combinatorics]], "for his fundamental contributions to graph theory, in particular for his work on structural aspects of graph theory, including solutions to Havel's 1969 problem and the Heckman–Thomas 14/5 problem on fractional colourings of cubic triangle-free graphs.<ref>{{citation|url=https://eurocomb2015.b.uib.no/eurocomb/the-european-prize-in-combinatorics/|title=The European Prize in Combinatorics|work=EuroComb 2015|publisher=University of Bergen|date=September 2015|access-date=2015-09-16|archive-date=2016-08-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820150918/https://eurocomb2015.b.uib.no/eurocomb/the-european-prize-in-combinatorics/|url-status=dead}}.</ref> This refers to two different results of Dvořák:
*Havel's conjecture is a strengthening of [[Grötzsch's theorem]]. It states that there exists a constant ''d'' such that, if a [[planar graph]] has no two triangles within distance ''d'' of each other, then it can be [[graph coloring|colored]] with three colors. A proof of this conjecture of Havel was announced by Dvořák and his co-authors in 2009.<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Dvořák | first1 = Zdeněk
 | last2 = Kráľ | first2 = Daniel | author2-link = Daniel Kráľ
 | last3 = Thomas | first3 = Robin | author3-link = Robin Thomas (mathematician)
 | arxiv = 0911.0885
 | title = Three-coloring triangle-free graphs on surfaces V. Coloring planar graphs with distant anomalies
 | year = 2009| bibcode = 2009arXiv0911.0885D}}.</ref>
*C. C. Heckman and [[Robin Thomas (mathematician)|Robin Thomas]] conjectured in 2001 that [[triangle-free graph]]s of maximum degree three have [[Fractional coloring|fractional chromatic number]] at most 14/5.<ref>{{citation

 | last2 = Thomas | first2 = Robin | author2-link = Robin Thomas (mathematician)

 | issue = 1–3
 | journal = [[Discrete Mathematics (journal)|Discrete Mathematics]]
 | mr = 1825617
 | pages = 233–237
 | title = A new proof of the independence ratio of triangle-free cubic graphs
 | volume = 233
 | year = 2001| doi-access = free
 }}.</ref> A proof was announced by Dvořák and his co-authors in 2013 and published by them in 2014.<ref>{{citation

 | last3 = Volec | first3 = J.

 | journal = [[Journal of the London Mathematical Society]]
